subject: Close timeline variance & mitigation options
messages:
From: Samantha O'Neil <samantha.oneil@pivotcloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: rajiv.menon@pivotcloud.com, procurement@pivotcloud.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Close window — procurement timing change

Kimberly — quick heads up from our side. Procurement has flagged a compliance review tied to our data residency appendix; they won't be able to sign off on the SOW this week.

We expect a formal hold until the vendor review finishes (~3 weeks), though the legal team said they may be able to provisionally approve commercial terms pending the residency appendix outcome.

What this means for us: the acceptance window in the MAP (target go-live 2027-05-01) is at risk. Can you share the minimal path to keep an initial rollout earlier (e.g., sandbox + limited seats) while we finish procurement? Also, any options on short-term credits or conditional milestones would help our CFO approve an interim commit.

I'll loop Rajiv and procurement. Happy to jump on a quick 20-minute call if helpful.

Thanks,
Samantha O'Neil
Head of Product Operations
PivotCloud

---
Attachment: vendor_review_summary.docx (stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Samantha O'Neil <samantha.oneil@pivotcloud.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@pivotcloud.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close window — procurement timing change

Samantha — thanks for the update and for flagging the residency hold. We anticipated a couple of procurement wrinkles on this account and have three pragmatic paths we can propose to keep momentum: 

1) Sandbox-first canary (preferred): We ship a scoped sandbox + 10 pilot seats by 2027-04-20 using existing standard terms; acceptance limited to functional tests until residency appendix clears.
2) Staged acceptance: Move final acceptance to a later date but execute a conditional go-live milestone in the MAP to enable early revenue recognition for a capped subset of workloads.
3) Full shift: Push final acceptance by 3 weeks and pause rollout gating (less desirable for your Q2 target).

I've attached an updated MAP with the sandbox-first option marked and responsibilities by week (MAP_v2.xlsx).

On credits: we can offer a one-time closing credit tied to final SOW execution (details in SOW_Redwood_draft_v3.pdf). We prefer to avoid open-ended discounts; instead we tie credits to acceptance milestones so both sides have runway protection.

Would you be available for a 20-minute call today at 4pm PT to walk through the sandbox scope and get procurement alignment? If not, suggest times tomorrow.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (updated MAP), SOW_Redwood_draft_v3.pdf (commercial draft)

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close window — procurement timing change

Following up with a quick risk snapshot and mitigation ladder we can present on the call: 

Risk log (short):
- Procurement appendix delay -> 2–3 week slip (probable)
- Scope creep during sandbox -> moderate
- Billing alignment (rev recognition) -> low-to-moderate

Mitigation ladder (recommended):
A) Sandbox-first: provide isolated sandbox environment (no PHI) + 10 pilot seats. Prep tasks: infra handoff (infra team), security checklist signoff (we pre-fill), truncated acceptance tests (QA).
B) Conditional SOW: add a milestone for 'Appendix-cleared acceptance' tying the credit to final sign-off (this protects revenue and gives PivotCloud runway).
C) Parallel legal/tech review: we offer a technical attestation document to procurement to speed the residency review (takes ~3 business days to produce).

I'll prepare the short attestation and update the MAP tasks to reflect parallel lanes. If procurement wants a 3-week shift, we recommend converting to a staged acceptance (A then B) versus a blunt reschedule so we retain early telemetry access.

--Priyom
Principal Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

---
Attachment: mitigation_ladder_onepager.pdf (stub)

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@pivotcloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Samantha O'Neil <samantha.oneil@pivotcloud.com>
Cc: procurement@pivotcloud.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close window — procurement timing change

Kimberly / Priyom — thanks for the thoughtful options. Procurement's position: the compliance group needs the residency appendix finalized before we can sign the SOW. Realistically, that pushes our final acceptance target by ~3 weeks (we're looking at a 2027-05-22 acceptance if the appendix clears on schedule).

That said, the product team supports a sandbox-first approach. Two asks before we lock into that route: 
1) Can Redwood commit to a temporary credit (applied if final SOW signs after the original target) tied to the delayed acceptance window? Our CFO needs a buffer for Q2 forecasting.
2) We need clarification on what telemetry and support we get during the sandbox — specifically, SLA levels, data deletion timeline, and whether sandbox logs are retained beyond 30 days.

If you can send the attestation doc and an updated MAP with sandbox obligations and the credit mechanics, we can expedite procurement once the appendix text is available.

Linking procurement for visibility.

Thanks,
Rajiv Menon
Director, Product Management — PivotCloud

---
Attachment: procurement_hold_form.pdf (stub)
Links: https://app.docusign.com/sandbox/placeholder-sign/abc123

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@pivotcloud.com>, Samantha O'Neil <samantha.oneil@pivotcloud.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 22:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close window — procurement timing change (escalation & exec ask)

Rajiv — appreciated. We will proceed with sandbox-first and formalize the conditional credit language tied to SOW execution after original target. Proposed next steps: 

1) I will send the technical attestation and an updated MAP (high level) by EOD Friday that lists deliverables for sandbox, telemetry commitments, retention windows, and acceptance criteria.
2) Priyom will prepare the attestation for procurement consumption (3 business days).
3) From Redwood: offer a one-time credit equal to 5% of the first 12 months' committed value if final SOW signs after 2027-05-01 (credit not to exceed $25k).

Flags for internal leadership: this is a Q2-close risk that could move ~40% of the ARR timing into late Q2. I'm copying Markus and Laura to request an executive alignment call if procurement refuses conditional acceptance and insists on a hard hold. We want to avoid a full pull on growth targets — sandbox-first preserves telemetry and early product feedback while protecting Redwood's economics via the capped credit.

Markus / Laura — can either of you join a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow 11am PT to confirm the credit authorization and exec talking points if the CFO pushes back?

Thanks all — I'll follow up with the MAP and attestation.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

---
Thread metadata note: internal escalation requested; follow-up items include MAP_v2 update, attestation doc, and credit approval.
